We checked “1023_SEMCO_OTHER_3984112_Overview_FS_TEMP_RES_PRINT” and found 7 issues in the InDesign file that are likely causing the problems in Frontify, plus 4 that may change how it looks. Here’s what to change:

Likely causing the problems

1. Kerning isn’t set to Metrics
Frontify spaces letters using the font’s own kerning (Metrics).
Where: the paragraph style “H4”, used on page 1
• In the paragraph style, go to Basic Character Formats and set Kerning to Metrics.
Learn more

2. Text frame has no paragraph style
Frontify uses paragraph styles to format text and decide what can be edited.
Where: text frames “SEMCO IQ flyer (868331)[TOP BANN…”, “15189510419” (page 1), “Date: File Name: Additional deta…”
• Select the frame and apply a paragraph style in Window > Styles > Paragraph Styles (any style except [Basic Paragraph] or [No Paragraph Style]).
Learn more

3. Font missing from the package
Frontify needs the font files to render the text, otherwise the template falls back to another font.
Where: fonts “Minion Pro” and “Times”
• Make sure the font is installed or activated on your computer.
• Package again with File > Package with "Copy Fonts" checked, and zip the whole folder, including "Document fonts".
Learn more

4. Items on a master page
Frontify only reads items on the document pages, so anything on a master page (called a parent page in newer InDesign versions) is ignored or breaks the template.
Found on the master page: 1 group
• In the Pages panel, open the master (parent) page and move its items onto the document pages, or delete them.
Learn more

5. Table in a text frame
Frontify doesn’t support InDesign tables.
Where: the text frame “Date: File Name: Additional deta…”
• Click into the table and choose Table > Convert Table to Text, or rebuild it with separate text frames.
Learn more

6. Text without a paragraph style
Frontify uses paragraph styles to format text and decide what can be edited.
Where: a text frame on page 1
• Select the text and apply a paragraph style in Window > Styles > Paragraph Styles (any style except [Basic Paragraph] or [No Paragraph Style]).
Learn more

7. Unsupported font format
Frontify can only use OpenType (.otf) and TrueType (.ttf) fonts.
Where: the font “Times.ttc”
• Get an OTF or TTF version from the font vendor and swap it in with Type > Find/Replace Font.
Learn more

May change how it looks

8. Text formatted outside its paragraph style
Formatting added by hand on top of a paragraph style (shown as a + next to the style name) may be lost or look different in Frontify.
Where: text frames “Start Saving See all the ways we…” (page 1, font, size, leading and more changed), “Residential No-cost Home Energy…” (page 1, tracking changed), “New construction rebates Energy…” (page 1, color changed) and 3 more
• Click into the text. A + after the style name in Window > Styles > Paragraph Styles means it has extra formatting.
• To remove it, select the text and click Clear Overrides at the bottom of the Paragraph Styles panel.
• To keep the look, update the style to match instead (right-click the style > Redefine Style), or use a character style for single words.
Learn more

9. Paragraph Composer used
The Adobe Paragraph Composer breaks lines differently from browsers, so text may reflow in Frontify.
Where: paragraph styles “H1”, “H2”, “Body” and 4 more, used on page 1
• In the paragraph style, go to Justification and set Composer to Adobe Single-line Composer.
Learn more

10. Baseline shift used
Frontify doesn’t support baseline shift, so shifted text sits on the baseline.
Where: the character style “[No character style]”
• Set Baseline Shift to 0 pt in the character style (Advanced Character Formats) or in the Character panel.
Learn more

11. Document has bleed
Bleed is added to every export, which is right for print templates but usually unwanted for digital ones.
Current bleed: 3.2 mm on all sides
• For a digital template, set bleed to 0 in File > Document Setup > Bleed and Slug. For print templates, bleed is fine.
Learn more

Worth a quick check (often fine as is)

12. Large image
Very large images slow down editing and exporting in Frontify.
Where: the image “iStock-1226023798.jpg” (page 1, 15.25 MB)
• Reduce the image’s pixel size or file size if it doesn’t need to be this large.
Learn more

Once that’s done, package the document again with File > Package, zip the package folder and upload it to Frontify.
